evidence: A dedicated Rust fixture and explicit opt-in systemd integration test demonstrated that a transient service survives launcher and MCP caller exit, retains a three-process tree including a setsid child in one cgroup, and kills the entire SIGTERM-resistant tree after TimeoutStopSec. A later cross-call probe matched InvocationID, ControlGroup, MainPID, process start ticks, and cgroup membership. Natural exit tests showed successful transient units may be garbage-collected while failed units retain exit evidence. The final persisted test log records 2 passed, 0 failed in 2.61 seconds with no residual units or fixture processes.
verification_result: The systemd/cgroup process-ownership model is locally proven for the current WSL boot. Recovery identity, lost/orphaned classification, boot-ID handling, and termination-intent interpretation are contract-tested. No production runner, persistent result, registry, capability evaluator, MCP Job tool, or deployment was implemented.
